                             Cool! Is it food safe?                                                         2 years ago

                                                                    35% Nepheline Syenite surely means this glaze crazes like...
                                                                                                 craze-y !?!? I've done a bowl in the blue version of this glaze
                                                                                     and heard it "tinging" away after I took it out of the (room
                                                                                                 temperature) kiln... I can't see the craze lines but assume
                                                                                                 they are there (indian ink might reveal?). Anyone experiencing
                                                                                                    crazing?

Rod Wren
                                                                                                            1 year ago

                                                                        David M. My understanding of what will determine
                                                                      whether it crazes or not is the ratio of Silica to Alumina
                                                                      from all the sources of those chemicals in the mix
                                                                                   (including the Nepheline Syenite) as well as the
                                                                           thermal expansion properties of your clay. Scroll down
                                                                                to see the UMF which shows for this glaze a ratio of
                                                                                    7.09:1 which will place itViewwellmorein the middle of the range,



                                                                                           Louise Shaw
                                                                             2 years ago

                                                         So if it runs too much you reduce the Boron,
                                                           add Titanium or Zirconium for opacity,
                                                            and Bentonite to help application ?


                                                                                  Will adding an opacifier to a floating base to make it more
                                                                        matt, not really work, so we need a different formula for a
                                                                  matt base ?
                                                                   Thanks, Louise



                                                                                      Matt Kanealii
                                                                         9 months ago

                                                                                                                                I have had limited success with this glaze…
                                                                    Crazing and lack of “blue float”. Looks good on dark clay.
                                                              Tends to go green on lighter clay where thin. Attempts to
                                                                          adjust away from GB have been difficult! Looks great in
                                                                   combination with Lynette’s opal and Steve Loucks opal.
                                                                     Continuing to pursue the grey purple and electric blue float!
